### AI in Nonprofit Fundraising: Key Trends and Insights for 2026

In 2026, AI adoption in nonprofit fundraising has surged to near-universal levels—**92% of nonprofits are using AI tools**—but real impact remains limited. A benchmark study of 346 nonprofits by Virtuous and Fundraising.AI shows **only 7% report major improvements in organizational capability**, highlighting an "efficiency plateau" where most gains are small to moderate (79%). The gap stems from isolated use (e.g., one person drafting appeals with ChatGPT) rather than team-wide workflow integration.

#### Practical AI Applications in Fundraising
Nonprofits are focusing on **time-saving tools** rather than replacing human relationships:
- **Content Creation**: AI drafts donor emails, appeals, impact updates, and event follow-ups in minutes. Staff review and personalize outputs for consistency (e.g., Giveffect reports this as the top use).
- **Administrative Efficiency**: Summarizes donor activity, automates reporting, and handles routine tasks like thank-you emails (via rule-based automation combined with AI).
- **Donor Prioritization**: Tools like Virtuous Momentum use AI to recommend daily donor outreach plans, draft personalized messages, and manage portfolios.
- **Predictive Insights**: 13% use AI for donor prospecting; smart donation forms boost average one-time gifts to $161 (vs. $115 industry average) and recurring gifts to $32 (vs. $24).

AI is embedded in CRMs (e.g., Virtuous, Salesforce) rather than standalone apps, emphasizing ethical use with human oversight.

#### Donor Behavior and Revenue Impact
- **Strategic Giving**: Donors favor fewer, larger gifts; monthly recurring donations drive sustainable revenue when intentional.
- **AI's Revenue Lift**: 30% of nonprofits report boosted fundraising revenue in the past year. Donors from AI chatbots (e.g., ChatGPT) give higher averages ($250) but convert slower.
- **Donor Sentiment**: 67% of online donors support AI in marketing/fundraising; 43% see positive/neutral effects on giving, though 31% are wary.
- **Challenges**: 60% lack in-house AI expertise; only 4% have AI training budgets. 23% of foundations reject AI-generated grant apps.

| Metric | Statistic | Source |
|--------|-----------|--------|
| AI Adoption | 92% using AI | Virtuous/Fundraising.AI 2026 Report |
| Major Impact | 7% see major capability gains | Virtuous/Fundraising.AI 2026 Report |
| Revenue Boost | 30% report fundraising increase | State of Nonprofit Digital Engagement |
| Top Uses | Productivity (35%), Marketing (31%), Fundraising (24%) | Center for Effective Philanthropy |
| Donor Approval | 67% OK with AI in tasks | Online Donor Feedback Survey 2025 |

#### Barriers to Impact and Best Practices
- **Common Pitfall**: Treating AI as a "workaround" instead of rethinking workflows (e.g., embedding AI agents team-wide).
- **Success Factors**: Set guardrails, integrate into CRMs, train staff (e.g., 2026 Certificate in AI for Marketing & Fundraising). Combine with transparency—now an operational must.
- **Ethical Focus**: 91% of funders expect positive AI impact; prioritize human-centered use to build trust.

**Predictions for 2026**: Growth in AI for donor-advised funds, asset-based giving, and real-time intelligence. Tools like Virtuous Insights and Fundraising.AI frameworks lead for scalable wins. For deeper dives, check the [2026 Nonprofit AI Adoption Report](https://virtuous.org/blog/2026-nonprofit-ai-adoption-report/) or [Giveffect Trends](https://www.giveffect.com/nonprofit-resource-center/2026-fundraising-trends-for-nonprofits-ai-donor-behavior-and-what-actually-matters/). Start small: Test AI drafting in your next campaign.
